daily.title: Berlin's punitive measures unlikely to deter Putin: experts
daily.summary: Germany has announced punitive measures after publicly blaming Russia for an attempted airport drone attack. But a former diplomat, political and security analysts warn it will likely do little to deter the Kremlin.

daily.title: Unity at last: Is Libya's damaging power struggle at an end?
daily.summary: For over a decade, Libya has been split between two opposing governments. Elections, meant to end the rivalry and unite the country, are now scheduled within two years.

daily.title: Germany: How to woo voters with an immigrant background
daily.summary: The number of voters in Germany with an immigrant background is rising. Yet the established parties barely manage to reach them. Why not?

daily.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
daily.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with King Charles and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

daily.title: Russia's hybrid attacks on Germany: When is it 'war?'
daily.summary: The German government is holding Russia responsible for an unsuccessful attack in Leipzig. Yet many feel that its response has been too mild.

daily.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
daily.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

daily.title: US sanctions halt TOEFL and GRE tests in Iran, disrupting study plans
daily.summary: Students in Iran can no longer take TOEFL and GRE exams after a US sanctions exemption was suspended. Applicants say the move threatens university deadlines and adds costly travel obligations.

daily.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy warns airlines to avoid Russian airspace
daily.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned a surge in Ukrainian drones in Russia's skies meant Russian airspace would be "effectively" closed. Meanwhile, Russian drones have hit Kyiv for a seventh straight day. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: Guinea-Bissau referendum tests democratic future
daily.summary: Following voter approval of a constitutional change that expands presidential powers, Guinea-Bissau faces renewed debate over legitimacy, civilian rule and democratic safeguards.

daily.title: India rejects Hague ruling on Indus waters: What's next?
daily.summary: By rejecting an international arbitration panel's ruling, New Delhi has cast fresh doubt on the future of the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty.

daily.title: Police exhume body of former Czechoslovak foreign minister Jan Masaryk
daily.summary: The top diplomat was found dead on March 10, 1948, in the courtyard beneath his bathroom window, supposedly after a fall. Police said their probe aims to settle questions that have surrounded the death ever since.

daily.title: Armed men abduct Kenyan editor, employer suspects government
daily.summary: A newspaper editor in Kenya was kidnapped from a car late on Tuesday and then located near a dam far away a few hours later. The Standard paper said it suspected state involvement in an attempt to intimidate reporters.

daily.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
daily.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

daily.title: What really helps Europe deal with drought
daily.summary: Fix leaks, or ban pools? As European countries prepare for hotter, drier years to come, here's what the data says about how to really save water.

daily.title: Charlie Kirk murder suspect to face potential death penalty
daily.summary: Tyler R., accused of fatally shooting Charlie Kirk, will stand trial on aggravated murder charges after a Utah judge ruled prosecutors had enough evidence to seek the death penalty.

daily.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
daily.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

daily.title: Cargo ship with 10 crew sinks off Turkey coast — authorities
daily.summary: Coast guard vessels and a helicopter are searching for 10 missing crew members off the coast of Istanbul. Authorities say they lost contact after the bulk carrier crashed into a chemical tanker off the coast of Istanbul.

daily.title: Germany news: Police probe suspected power station attacks
daily.summary: Police are investigating after homemade projectiles were used to damage power lines in eastern Germany. This comes amid suspicion of sabotage at another power station in the west of the country. DW has more.

daily.title: Tunisia's activists decry civil society crackdown
daily.summary: Five years into Tunisian President Kais Saied’s increasingly authoritarian rule, rights groups warn that the country’s once vibrant civil society is being silenced.

daily.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty to collusion
daily.summary: The prominent activist pleaded guilty to colluding with foreign entities. He faces a lengthy prison sentence.

daily.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
daily.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

daily.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
daily.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

weekly.title: Germany terminates lease for Berlin's Russian House
weekly.summary: Germany has announced the termination of the lease for the Russian House in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it is a hub for propaganda and espionage.

weekly.title: As glaciers melt, can communities be protected?
weekly.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

weekly.title: Mladic's death, Bosnia and Serbia's unfinished reckoning
weekly.summary: The death of Ratko Mladic did not close a dark chapter of European history; it reopened old wounds. The ideology that created him lives on. The Dayton peace agreement ended the war, not the divisions that produced it.

weekly.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII takes oath in parliament
weekly.summary: The new king swore to uphold the constitution in parliament in Oslo, the first major institutional step of his reign. Haakon VIII's wife Queen Mette-Marit had to skip the event in the aftermath of her lung transplant.

weekly.title: Germany's center-left SPD is fighting for survival
weekly.summary: The Social Democratic Party is sinking ever deeper into crisis. Voters are turning away, while unrest is growing within its grassroots ranks. Will upcoming state elections accelerate the party's downward spiral?

weekly.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
weekly.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor Canada.

weekly.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
weekly.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

weekly.title: Ulrich Siegmund wants to make Saxony-Anhalt a model for AfD rule
weekly.summary: The AfD's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund aims to turn his small federal state into a blueprint for right-wing extremist politics across Germany.

weekly.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
weekly.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

weekly.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
weekly.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt State Premier Schulze takes on far-right AfD
weekly.summary: The AfD is far ahead in the polls in Saxony-Anhalt. But Schulze is determined to keep the AfD from becoming the first far-right party since World War II to lead a German state government.

weekly.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
weekly.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

weekly.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
weekly.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

weekly.title: Germany news: Summer was 2nd hottest of the century — DWD
weekly.summary: Germany's DWD weather service says the summer was second only to 2003 in terms of average temperatures. It was also unusually dry. In Cologne, police are seeking a man who fired shots at a cafe storefront.

weekly.title: Fact check: Germany's Merz misstates record in ARD interview
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made several misleading claims on migration, debt and electric vehicles in his summer interview with German public broadcaster ARD.

weekly.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire

weekly.title: Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas

weekly.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers

weekly.title: Serbia keeps EU, Russia in play ahead of key election

weekly.title: Germany's military wants to recruit tech-savvy gamers

weekly.summary: The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.

weekly.summary: Official polling suggests public sentiment in Russia is deteriorating as economic pressure builds. DW asked its users to share their experiences.

weekly.summary: From works of "self-obliteration" to polka dotted nudes, the pioneering artist developed a unique body of work likely to be relevant for years to come.
